text: 📸 Inauguración de la Universidad Nacional Rosario Castellanos, plantel Nicolás Romero — Estado de México, 11 de octubre de 2026

🇲🇽🎨 "Since then I've thought that education is the heart of the country's transformation." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Rosario Castellanos National University, Nicolás Romero, State of Mexico Forty years ago, as a physics student at UNAM, she represented the Faculty of Sciences in the Consejo Estudiantil Universitario (CEU). The rector had raised fees — "Education has to be paid for so that students value it" — and moved to end automatic admission from UNAM's high schools. Students from UNAM, the Poli and other universities marched to the Zócalo, and the reforms were rolled back. "That's why the National Autonomous University of Mexico is practically free." Rector Jorge Carpizo's 1986 reforms were suspended after the CEU strike of early 1987.

🇲🇽✊ "When Hidalgo cries out for independence, a few days later he says, 'Slavery must be abolished.' And a few days after that: 'The castes must disappear. All of us are equal.'" — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Rosario Castellanos National University, Nicolás Romero, State of Mexico Speaking to incoming students, she began with the machista advice she grew up with — don't tell your age, "calladita te ves más bonita." "Not anymore. Women look prettier when we speak and when we participate." Then she walked through the colonial caste system and Morelos' Sentimientos de la Nación: "To this day there are still those who believe there are castes in our country, but no. All Mexicans are equal before the law.

🇲🇽🎨 "Now that I'm president I said: we have to build more high schools and more universities." — Presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum, Rosario Castellanos National University, Nicolás Romero, State of Mexico The goal: enough new high schools for another 400,000 young people nationwide, and university places for about 350,000 — "I think it will be more, because we're already at about 250,000 across all the public universities." In Nicolás Romero 800 students got in and 400 more will study online, so a Margarita Maza high school and an expansion of the campus are coming. University students also get the new Gertrudis Bocanegra scholarship, a support equal to the Benito Juárez grant in high school. "Nothing gives me more joy than cutting the ribbon of a free public university."

🇲🇽✊ "For a long time the neoliberal discourse was always that we had no right to a degree if we weren't born somewhere with a university nearby, no right to study if we didn't have the money to do it." "Today every one of us here who is a student has the chance to not have to choose between working and studying, between spending on bus fare or spending on our food." — Jessica Olmos Ruiz, psychology student, Rosario Castellanos National University, Nicolás Romero She spoke for the incoming class at the campus opening. "It's also an honor to see that the three people who represent us at the national, state and municipal level are women" — President Sheinbaum, Governor Delfina Gómez and Mayor Joseline Mendoza.

🇲🇽🎨 "It was not until the Fourth Transformation of Mexico's public life that higher education stopped being a commodity and became not only a right, but the enormous possibility we Mexicans have to imagine a country based on social justice, equity, collective well-being and shared prosperity." — Alma Herrera Márquez, rector of the Rosario Castellanos National University, Nicolás Romero She spoke at the opening of the university's new campus in Nicolás Romero, State of Mexico, on October 11. 800 students start classes next week in seven degree programs; applicants from the municipality saturated the registration system in four days. The municipal government built the buildings; the university supplies the faculty. The Rosario Castellanos now has more than 122,000 students, 45,508 of them enrolled in 2026.

🇲🇽✈️ <u>US Airlines Cut 435,000 Seats to Mexico's Caribbean</u>

US flights into Cancún, Cozumel and Tulum shrink 12.8% in seats and 13.3% in flights for October–December: more than 435,000 seats and 2,600 flights gone after Spirit's exit and cuts by other carriers, per the Anáhuac Cancún STARC Travel Sentiment Index reported by El Economista. Canada moves the other way: +5.5% in seats, with Porter Airlines entering. Between January and August, the drop in US visitors already cost Quintana Roo 707,000 room-nights.

🇲🇽🏗️ <u>Tlaxcala: 7,000 Public Works in Five Years, Zero Debt</u>

Tlaxcala Governor Lorena Cuéllar marked five years of the Fourth Transformation in the state with more than 7,000 public works across all 60 municipalities, on a limited budget and without contracting public debt. The list: a new General Hospital replacing one that was 77 years old, 15 new medical facilities, 30 new secondary schools, 10 universities, and over 58,000 housing, basic-services and social-support actions. A Regional Specialty Hospital is next.

🇲🇽🇵🇸 <u>Palestine's Ambassador Leads Mexico City March for Gaza</u>

Palestinian Ambassador to Mexico Nadya Rasheed marched from Paseo de la Reforma to the Alameda Central alongside a family exiled from Gaza, anti-Zionist Jewish organizations and some thousand demonstrators. Organizers said 59 other cities joined the Global Day of Action. The demands: an immediate ceasefire in Gaza, and for the Mexican government to break relations with Israel. In San Cristóbal de Las Casas, Chiapas, actress Ofelia Medina and singer Rubén Albarrán joined the call to stop the genocide.
banner: CDMX MARCHES FOR GAZA WITH 59 CITIES

🚨🇲🇽 <u>No T-MEC Deal Before the US Midterms, Johns Hopkins Economist Warns</u>

Mexico should not expect a trade deal with Washington before November. A Johns Hopkins economist told La Jornada: "There is no possibility of an agreement before the November elections. Definitely not." The easy chapters are closed. What's left is the hard part: regional content in strategic sectors and US proposals to restrict Chinese investment in Mexico. Even with a signed deal, the White House can still impose unilateral tariffs. "The baseline of tariffs has already changed." Canada already got last-minute conditions.
banner: T-MEC: NO DEAL BEFORE US MIDTERMS
